title: Fresh starts
hookLine: people start new habits more often after a birthday, a Monday, a new month (Dai, Milkman and Riis)

lines: A MONDAY. A BIRTHDAY. A NEW JOB.
cards: New Year's Day. A Monday. The morning after a birthday.
The first day at a new job. On mornings like these, promises seem easier to make, and gyms seem a little busier.
Three researchers, Hengchen Dai, Katherine Milkman and Jason Riis, wondered whether that was real or just a feeling.
So they looked at what people searched for online, how often people went to a university gym, and when people signed up to commit to goals. The pattern they found got a name of its own.

teach.b: First, the finding. Searches for the word 'diet,' gym visits and goal commitments all rose after what the researchers called temporal landmarks: the start of a new week, a new month, a new year, a birthday, a holiday.
They named it the fresh start effect. Second, the why.

teach.h: A LINE IN THE STORY OF YOURSELF.
teach.b: Their explanation is that landmarks draw a line in the story people tell about themselves. The person who skipped the gym belongs to last month.

The new month seems to belong to someone a little different, and that bit of distance makes starting feel possible. Third, the honest edge. A fresh start is a moment to begin, not a promise of finishing.
And there's a quiet trap in waiting for one: Monday becomes a reason not to start on Thursday.
A landmark helps most when it's used, not waited for. Fourth, an old line about new mornings. The book of Lamentations, in the Hebrew Bible, is a book of grief over a ruined city.

In the middle of it, the writer says of the Lord's mercies: 'They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.' Jews and Christians both read those words. They point to something the research also hints at.
A fresh start doesn't need January. Every morning is already a small landmark, and so is this breath.

how: People who use the fresh start effect often tie a new practice to the next natural landmark, such as a Monday, the first of the month or a birthday, and treat each morning as a smaller one.

o: wiping out every past habit and beginning from zero
a vacation taken to rest before a big change
landmarks like a new week that make starting feel easier

games.q: inside fresh starts: tap the pairs.
p: a new week, month or birthday

s: gym visits rose after landmarks like a new week
the researchers found visits, searches and goal sign-ups rose after landmarks.
a fresh start guarantees the habit sticks
it's a moment to begin, not a promise of finishing.
fresh starts only happen on New Year's Day

games.q: it's thursday, and you want to begin a morning sit. what fits today's lesson best?
o: wait for monday so it feels clean.
use tomorrow morning as your landmark.
games.why: landmarks help, and a morning can be one. waiting past the nearest landmark only delays the start.

practice: Pick your next fresh start, large like the first of next month, or small like tomorrow morning or the moment this sit ends, and one small thing to begin there. Then let the plan rest.
Spend the sit with the breath, treating each breath as a small fresh start of its own.

wordCard.voice: Fresh starts. People begin new habits more often after landmarks: a Monday, a new month, a birthday. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: a fresh start. The mornings keep arriving, one after another. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.ref: Dai, Milkman & Riis, "The fresh start effect: Temporal landmarks motivate aspirational behavior"

sources.q: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
